nodes.name: Decide Retry Timing
nodes.notes: Maps failure_reason to RETRY delay or CUSTOMER_ACTION. Unknown reasons require customer action.

parameters.content:
## Load Due Retries

Every 15 minutes we open the retry queue. We keep only payments that are due now and still allowed to retry. Payments that already succeeded, need customer action, or hit the limit are skipped.

## Receive Failed Payment

When a payment fails, the details arrive here first. We clean and organize the information so the rest of the workflow can use it safely. No card numbers or secret codes are stored.

## Prevent Duplicates
We check if this same failure was already saved in the sheet. If it was, we mark it as a duplicate. This stops the same event from creating two retry records.

## Duplicate Stop

This failure was already handled before. We do not add another row or send another email. The workflow simply stops for this event.

## Retry or Notify Customer

Based on why the payment failed, we decide whether to try again later or ask the customer to fix their payment method. Auto-retries are saved in the queue with a wait time. If the customer must act, we save that status and send them an email.

## Failure Path

The retry did not work. If tries remain, we set a new retry time in the same sheet row. If no tries remain, we mark it as failed and email the customer to update their payment method or contact support.

## Attempt Payment Retry

We handle each due payment one by one. We call the payment service to charge again, then read whether it worked. When every due payment is checked, this run is finished.

## Success Path

The retry was successful. We update the sheet to show success and stop further retries. Then we email the customer to confirm their payment went through.

# Intelligent Retry Timing Optimizer

This workflow receives failed payment events, decides whether to auto-retry or ask the customer to act, stores retries in Google Sheets, retries due payments every 15 minutes through an HTTP payment API, and emails customers on success, action needed, or final failure.

## How it works

When a payment fails, this workflow receives the failure details and decides what to do next. Soft problems (like insufficient funds or temporary bank errors) are saved in a Google Sheet retry queue with a smart wait time—about 3 days, 2 hours, or 1 hour depending on the reason. Hard problems (expired card, invalid card, extra login needed, or fraud) are not auto-retried; the customer is emailed to update their payment method instead. The same failure event is never saved twice.

Every 15 minutes, the second part of the workflow checks the queue for payments that are due. It retries each one through the payment API. If the payment succeeds, the sheet is updated and the customer gets a success email. If it fails again, another retry is scheduled—or, after the maximum attempts, the customer is told the payment could not be completed.

## Setup steps

**1.** Create a Google Sheet with a tab named RetryQueue and the required column headers.
**2.** Connect your Google Sheets and Gmail accounts in n8n.
**3.** Replace YOUR_GOOGLE_SHEET_ID in every Google Sheets node.
**4.** Set the payment retry HTTP node to your real (or test) payment API URL and auth.
**5.** Activate the workflow, then send a test failed-payment to the webhook to confirm it runs.
